I was born and raised in a small town, the middle child of three siblings. My parents were hardworking individuals who instilled in me the values of determination and perseverance. As a child, I was always curious about the world around me, asking questions and seeking answers. This curiosity led me to develop a love for learning, which has stayed with me throughout my life.

In high school, I was involved in various extracurricular activities, including the debate team and the science club. I also had a part-time job at a local bookstore, where I discovered my passion for literature. My love for books eventually inspired me to pursue a degree in English Literature in college.

During my college years, I was an active member of the student body, serving as the president of the English Honor Society and volunteering at a local literacy program. I also had the opportunity to study abroad in London, where I immersed myself in the city's rich literary history.

After graduation, I worked as a copywriter for a marketing firm. While I enjoyed the creative aspect of the job, I found myself longing for something more meaningful. I decided to quit my job and join the Peace Corps, where I spent two years teaching English in a rural village in Africa.

My experience in the Peace Corps was life-changing. It taught me the importance of empathy, compassion, and resilience. I learned to adapt to new cultures, communicate with people from different backgrounds, and find solutions to complex challenges.

Upon my return to the United States, I pursued a master's degree in Education. I became a teacher and have been teaching high school English for the past ten years. In my classroom, I strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment where students feel valued and heard. I believe that education is not just about imparting knowledge but also about fostering critical thinking skills, creativity, and emotional intelligence.

Outside of the classroom, I enjoy reading, writing, and hiking. I am also an avid traveler, having visited over thirty countries. I believe that traveling broadens one's perspective and promotes tolerance and understanding.

Throughout my life, I have faced many challenges and obstacles, but I have always remained true to myself and my values. I am grateful for the opportunities I have had and the people I have met along the way. I look forward to continuing my journey of learning and growth, making a positive impact on those around me, and striving to be the best version of myself.
